general.advice: Evaluate immediate damage, control of multiple enemies, defense, long-fight scaling and access to the right cards. A rare payoff can lose to an ordinary card that solves the next encounter. An established package does not excuse an unanswered threat; compatible packages can coexist.

Draw, removal and manipulation help align useful cards with the turn that needs them. Count draw and energy opportunity costs when adding another damage or setup card. Judge a card's remaining job rather than its isolated strength.

A combat card reward costs no gold but does consume future draws. Compare the best offered card with adding nothing: take it when it answers a current threat or adds a reliable needed job; skip marginal, redundant or unsupported additions. Early damage can be essential, so neither a fixed skip rate nor a target deck size is sound.

Each addition can delay access and redraw of key cards; removal and real draw effects can improve access. Still compare damage frontload, sustained scaling and defensive coverage: a smaller deck that lacks an upcoming fight's answer is worse. Power and Exhaust change later-cycle size, while status-heavy enemies can make a larger deck useful.

Once stronger cards cover a starter's job, removing that starter can make the useful cards recur more reliably. Low-impact early attacks can obstruct later defense and setup. Compare the exact card lost with the retained cards reached more often; early damage that still solves an upcoming fight remains valuable.

Treat paid card removal as a real shop purchase, especially when starter cards or curses have become dead draws. Compare the retained deck's repeated access with each offered item and the exact gold budget. A purchase that leaves enough gold for removal can be taken first; a purchase that prevents removal must justify giving it up.

Strike versus Defend is a current-deck comparison, not a character-wide fixed order. Upgrades, enchantments, existing replacements and supported Strike or curse payoffs can change the answer. Compare removal with the actual shop offers and prices; neither removing at every shop nor achieving a fixed small deck size is mandatory.

Use the revealed boss and reachable paths to evaluate preparation needs. Elite rewards compete with HP, potions and access to rest or upgrades. Preserve route flexibility where useful. A question-mark node does not guarantee a safe room, and a suggested elite count is not a rule.

IRONCLAD.overview: Healing can support useful HP trades, but it does not prevent lethal damage. Early standalone damage need not commit the deck to that attack's eventual package.

packages.requires: Repeatable Vulnerable application and attacks or debuff payoffs.
packages.tradeoff: Apply before beneficiaries when useful; evaluate actual stacks, cost and immunity.

packages.requires: Exhaust outlets plus useful triggers or a better remaining deck.
packages.tradeoff: Removing cards also removes future defense and damage; setup needs time.

packages.requires: Sufficient Block generation and a way to convert or preserve it.
packages.tradeoff: Retention setup without generation may be too slow.

packages.requires: A supported self-loss trigger and useful payoff.
packages.tradeoff: Budget actual HP and setup cost; healing is not guaranteed in time.

packages.requires: Draw and compatible Strike effects.
packages.tradeoff: A standalone early attack does not justify every later Strike reward.

SILENT.overview: Damage, discard, Poison and Shiv tools can complement each other. Pick the pieces that fix current output or consistency rather than forcing a pure archetype.

packages.requires: Reliable discard outlets and enough flow to meet the payoff cards.
packages.tradeoff: A discard payoff without its outlet can be a dead draw; extra copies can exceed available discard.

packages.requires: Generation, useful attack triggers and enough hand space.
packages.tradeoff: Per-play or per-hit retaliation changes the cost of many small attacks.

packages.requires: Application and defense until the relevant poison timing.
packages.tradeoff: Slow damage must still solve the current enemy response and multi-enemy pressure.

packages.requires: Application on enemies whose damage matters.
packages.tradeoff: Debuff support complements rather than replaces damage and card flow.

REGENT.overview: Track Stars separately from energy. A large stored reserve and sustainable generation are different resources; repeated spenders need future supply. Forge, Stars and draw control can be combined when their costs fit.

packages.requires: Generation and worthwhile spenders over multiple deck cycles.
packages.tradeoff: A good energy ratio can hide a Star shortage. Retain defense while investing in generation.

packages.requires: Forging plus repeated access to the Blade.
packages.tradeoff: Retain keeps an unplayed Blade; after playing it, retrieval or another draw is needed.

packages.requires: A useful redraw payoff and ways to control access.
packages.tradeoff: Deck manipulation uses resources before the payoff arrives.

NECROBINDER.overview: Consider the player's HP, Osty's current HP, damage timing and draw access together. A delayed kill needs an answer to attacks that occur before execution.

packages.requires: Summoning and attacks that use Osty effectively.
packages.tradeoff: Spending Osty's HP as defense can change subsequent attack value; verify current native values.

packages.requires: Enough application and defense until the actual execution condition.
packages.tradeoff: Use the current rule's threshold and timing; Doom is not immediate attack damage.

packages.requires: Generation and useful cards or triggers reached through drawing.
packages.tradeoff: Extra access needs energy or low-cost follow-through; generated cards need observation.

packages.requires: Effects that benefit from playing or exhausting the relevant cards.
packages.tradeoff: Compare keeping access with the timing of exhaustion and its triggers.

DEFECT.overview: Orb plans and low-cost attack plans need different support. Evaluate current channeling rate, slots, orb order, passive timing and energy before choosing a scaling direction.

packages.requires: Channeling plus appropriate output scaling or evocation.
packages.tradeoff: Extra slots only help when filled; they delay evocation. Frost can support defense, while other orb plans need another defense source. Focus does not improve Plasma.

packages.requires: Repeated access to useful low-cost attacks.
packages.tradeoff: Cheap cards still consume draws and can incur reaction damage.

packages.requires: An attack pool that supports the intended chain.
packages.tradeoff: Unwanted attacks can disrupt the chain; account for the cost of shaping the deck.

packages.requires: Status generation with a supported payoff.
packages.tradeoff: Without the payoff in time, statuses obstruct useful draws.
